svg.title: P018 · Customers with no order in the last 90 days
svg.desc: One row per customer without an order in the 90-date window. The latest order is March 31. January 1 through March 31 inclusive covers ninety dates. Asha matches order 10. Ben's order is too old and Cia has no order. All three customers remain, with two empty right sides. Asha leaves because her match has ID 10. Ben and Cia both have a NULL matched order ID. Ben (ID 2) signed up before Cia (ID 3). Both qualify even though their order histories differ.
svg.text: Customers with no order in the last 90 days
One row per customer without an order in the 90-date window.
Ben has an old order and Cia has none. Should they reach the same result?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Double underlines mark the matching keys. SQL excerpts use … for
How do we find the ninety calendar dates?
The latest order is March 31. January 1 through March 31 inclusive covers ninety dates.
Why put the order-date condition inside ON?

Customers LEFT JOIN Orders ON Customers.CustomerID = Orders.CustomerID AND date(Orders.OrderDate) BETWEEN …
Which joined rows prove there was no recent order?
Asha leaves because her match has ID 10. Ben and Cia both have a NULL matched order ID.
How does the outreach list read?
Ben (ID 2) signed up before Cia (ID 3). Both qualify even though their order histories differ.
